newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble eases on bearish selling, position-closing.
newsitem.headline: Rouble eases on bearish selling, position-closing.

text.p: The rouble eased in calm trading on Tuesday on speculative selling and position-squaring by banks, dealers said.
"The market is calm today, overnight rouble credit rates were higher in the morning as banks were trading on their own interests but it was not a trend," Avtobank dealer Sergei Gornev said.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 25-35 percent compared with an early 40-50 percent and Monday's late 5-15 percent.

Another dealer said rouble/dollar rates had edged down from early levels on speculative selling by some operators. He added overnight credit rates remained relatively high ahead of Wednesday's government bond auctions.
But Gornev said: "The auctions have nothing to do with it, otherwise rates would have been much higher."
On September 18 the central bank is auctioning 7.5 trillion roubles of six-month T-bills and two trillion roubles of an additional tranche of a two-year OFZ interest-bearing bond.
Previously rouble credit rates would jump to 100 percent or more ahead of the auctions but fall to 5-10 percent afterwards.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,382-85 per dollar compared with an early 5,379-81 and 5,376-79 late on Monday. Tomorrow roubles eased to 5,388-91 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,382-85.
The central bank said it had set 5,356/5,396 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Tuesday.
